name: ruby-lsp-rs
description: Ruby language support powered by ruby-lsp-rs: a Rust port of Ruby LSP with Steep-compatible type inference, type inlay hints, hover and diagnostics.

rubyLspRs.server.path.markdownDescription: Path to the `ruby-lsp-rs` server executable. When empty, the extension looks for the `RUBY_LSP_RS_SERVER_PATH` environment variable, then the server bundled in the extension (`server/ruby-lsp-rs`), then `ruby-lsp-rs` on `PATH`. Relative paths are resolved against the first workspace folder. Changing this setting requires a server restart.

rubyLspRs.server.extraEnv.markdownDescription: Extra environment variables that will be passed to the server executable. Useful for passing e.g. `RUST_LOG` for debugging. Changing this setting requires a server restart.

rubyLspRs.rubyCommand.markdownDescription: Command used by the server to run Ruby, e.g. to detect the Bundler environment. Given as an array of the executable and its arguments, such as `["mise", "exec", "--", "ruby"]`, `["rbenv", "exec", "ruby"]` or `["asdf", "exec", "ruby"]`. When empty, the command is detected from the workspace (`.tool-versions`, `mise.toml`, `.mise.toml` with mise, `.ruby-version` with rbenv) and falls back to `ruby` on `PATH`. Changing this setting requires a server restart.

rubyLspRs.typeChecker.enable.markdownDescription: Whether to enable type inference and type checking based on RBS signatures.

rubyLspRs.typeChecker.diagnostics.enable.markdownDescription: Whether to show type errors as diagnostics. Has no effect when `#rubyLspRs.typeChecker.enable#` is disabled.

rubyLspRs.definition.target.markdownDescription: Where Go to Definition (Cmd/Ctrl+Click) jumps for methods and constants, and where Go to Type Definition jumps for the classes in the type of a variable or an expression. The RBS signature is always available from Go to Declaration and from the links in the hover.
enumDescriptions: Jump to the Ruby implementation found from the inferred receiver type. Falls back to the RBS signature when there is no Ruby implementation, e.g. core methods written in C
Show both the Ruby implementation and the RBS signature

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.methodReturnTypes.e.markdownDescription: Whether to show inlay type hints for the return types of method definitions.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.methodParameterType.markdownDescription: Whether to show inlay type hints for the parameters of method definitions.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.attributeTypes.enab.markdownDescription: Whether to show inlay type hints for attributes defined with `attr_reader`, `attr_writer` and `attr_accessor`.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.variableTypes.enabl.markdownDescription: Whether to show inlay type hints for variables.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.blockParameterTypes.markdownDescription: Whether to show inlay type hints for block parameters.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.hideObviousTypes.markdownDescription: Whether to hide inlay type hints when the type is obvious from the right-hand side, e.g. literals and `Foo.new`.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.hideUntyped.markdownDescription: Whether to hide inlay type hints whose type is `untyped`.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.maxLength.markdownDescription: Maximum length for inlay type hints. Set to `null` to have an unlimited length.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.implicitRescue.enab.markdownDescription: Whether to show inlay hints for the implicit `StandardError` of bare `rescue` clauses. Changing this setting requires a server restart.

rubyLspRs.inlayHints.implicitHashValue.e.markdownDescription: Whether to show inlay hints for omitted hash values (e.g. `{ name: }`). Changing this setting requires a server restart.

rubyLspRs.formatter.markdownDescription: Which tool the server should use for formatting files. Changing this setting requires a server restart.

rubyLspRs.linters.markdownDescription: List of linter tools that the server should use for diagnostics, e.g. `["rubocop_internal"]`. When `null`, linters are detected automatically. Changing this setting requires a server restart.

rubyLspRs.enabledFeatures.markdownDescription: Enable or disable individual language server features. The feature names are the same as `rubyLsp.enabledFeatures` of the Ruby LSP extension. Changing this setting requires a server restart.

codeActions.description: Enable code actions, like RuboCop quick fixes.

documentHighlights.description: Enable document highlights, which highlight the occurrences of the symbol at the cursor position.

documentLink.description: Enable document links, which generate clickable links to 'PATH' based on '# source://PATH' comments.

documentSymbols.description: Enable document symbols, which populate the file outline and breadcrumbs.

foldingRanges.description: Enable folding ranges, which populate the places where code can be folded.

hover.description: Enable hover, which displays a widget with extra information when hovering over code.

selectionRanges.description: Enable selection ranges, which select code based on the position of the cursor(s).

semanticHighlighting.description: Enable semantic highlighting, which highlights code based on Ruby's understanding of it.

completion.description: Enable completion, which provides suggestions for code completion.

codeLens.description: Enable code lens, which generates clickable text to enrich the editor experience.

definition.description: Enable go to definition, which navigates to the definition of the symbol under the cursor.

workspaceSymbol.description: Enable workspace symbol, which allows fuzzy searching for symbols in the entire project.

signatureHelp.description: Enable signature help, which shows the parameters and documentation of the method being invoked.

typeHierarchy.description: Enable type hierarchy, which shows the supertypes and subtypes of the selected symbol.

rubyLspRs.trace.server.markdownDescription: Trace the communication between VS Code and the language server.
